title: Decision-safety saga for canary commit with audit-playback
author: Jordan Patel
description:
Motivation: Build a lightweight saga-style rollback orchestration layer for canary commits that coordinates cross-service compensation actions, provides an auditable playback for incident repro, and exposes staged decision points for human escalation. Many existing controllers handle traffic phasing and metric gates; this PR focuses on the commit/compensate lifecycle and forensic replay so on-call can reproduce and unwind complex promotes across model variants and downstream transforms.

What this PR adds: a) a SagaExecutor component that records atomic commit steps (traffic transition, KV migration, cache invalidation, feature-flag flips) and associated compensation actions; b) decision checkpoints wired to telemetry gates (latency/error/qa-regressions) that can auto-run compensations or escalate to a human reviewer; c) a synthetic-smoke runner that executes a configurable suite of synthetic requests against the canary variant and stores trace-correlated snapshots; d) an audit-playback tool that replays recorded traffic slices deterministically in a sandboxed dry-run to reproduce observed regressions; e) a compact JSON-based saga journal (append-only) with signatures for forensic integrity and optional encryption hooks for Private deployments.

Design notes: the saga journal is append-only and arranged as discrete steps with idempotency keys to allow safe retries. The SagaExecutor exposes a finite-state machine: PREPARE -> EXECUTE_STEP -> CHECKPOINT -> ON_FAILURE -> COMPENSATE -> COMPLETE. Checkpoints evaluate telemetry rules (configured with SLO thresholds and rate-aware heuristics). If a checkpoint is tripped, the executor will first attempt automated compensation and then open a human review ticket when configured thresholds are exceeded. The audit-playback replays in a constrained environment: synthetic smoke first, then traffic-replay with session affinity preserved if available.

Rollout safety: to avoid split-brain between autoscaling and staged promote we added a lease token per saga commit; only the token-holder may mark a saga as COMPLETE. Leases are short-lived and renewed automatically; orphaned leases trigger a conservative auto-compensate path.

Backward compatibility: defaults keep existing rollout controllers intact. The SagaExecutor is opt-in per rollout via a single flag in the rollout spec: "saga: enabled", and an optional "audit_playback: enabled" flag for environments that allow replay.

Checklist: - [x] Saga journal schema and migrations - [x] SagaExecutor FSM and API surface - [x] Telemetry gate integration and SLO mapping - [x] Synthetic-smoke runner and CI harness - [x] Audit-playback CLI and sandbox mode - [x] Tests: unit + integration + a replay smoke test in staging - [x] Docs: rollout cookbook and runbook snippets

Impact: Intended to improve on-call confidence for staged promotions by enabling deterministic repro and safe cross-service unwind. It provides a clear audit trail for compliance and a programmable way to encode compensations for complicated model swaps.
commits_summary: 3 main commits + fixes: 1) core saga executor, state machine and journal writer; 2) telemetry gate adapter and SLO rule mapping; 3) audit-playback CLI and sandbox harness; followed by two patches addressing flaky synthetic smoke tests and a README update for rollout docs.
review_comments: Nina Kapoor: Nice shape. A couple of concerns: the lease renewal relies on the same RPC channel as the executor — what happens if the node is partitioned? Can we push lease renewal into our existing lease-manager (suggested change)?
Jordan Patel: Good catch — moved lease renewals to the existing lease-manager service and added a fast-fail conservative compensation if renewal fails for >2x lease interval.

Ethan Shaw: The audit-playback replayed 1k sessions in staging and we saw an intermittent NPE in transform_v2 when session affinity is missing. Suggest adding a defensive shim in transform_v2 and a fallback session bucket.
Jordan Patel: Added shim and updated playback to preserve affinity when available; added integration test that toggles affinity on/off.
Priya Kumar: Small nit: the saga journal needs schema version bump handling in upgrades; otherwise migrations could shadow older journals.
Jordan Patel: Added migration script v1->v2 and migration test; documented the upgrade path in the runbook.
Nina Kapoor: Approved after lease-manager and migration tests were green.
ci_checks: integration-tests: fail (initial run) - synthetic smoke flaky on timing-sensitive fixtures
release_notes: Adds an opt-in saga-style rollback orchestration for staged canary commits, telemetry gate integration, synthetic smoke runner, and audit-playback tool for deterministic replay. Opt-in via rollout spec flag 'saga.enabled'.
